definition.label: Begging the question
definition.definition: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.

source.currentDescription: Carrier interprets authentic epistles as describing a revealed celestial being before later literary gospels place Jesus in history, with subsequent attestation dependent on those narratives.
source.lockedProposition: The epistles present a celestial revealed being before later crafted gospels place Jesus in history.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: also our sequence of evidence corresponds to it the epistles the reliable epistles or i should say the seven authentic epistles of paul they only speak of a celestial being and a revealed gospel i'll get to that in a moment the gospels come decades later and they are well-crafted literary fictions we actually have numerous scholars who've published books uh i give a lot of evidence myself and and collect a lot of this in my book on the historicity of jesus showing that their very structure of the gospels is literary it serves particular allegorical functions all later historicity claims are based on the gospels we have no evidence of any other historian that includes josephus tacitus or anyone else having sources other than the gospels or christians citing the gospels we can't establish there's any independent corroboration so everything seems to come from the gospels when they were written and first put jesus in history
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Carrier clearly sequences seven authentic Pauline epistles before the literary gospels, connecting chronology to his central development claim that later historicity reports depend upon gospel tradition rather than independent corroboration. Principal limitation: Literary construction does not establish invention, while exclusively celestial Pauline language and universal dependence by Josephus, Tacitus, or later witnesses are asserted categorically despite disputed interpretations. Live burden: Opposition must identify independent attestation or earthly Pauline referents, but Carrier must demonstrate the developmental mechanism by which revelation became biography and engage mixed readings rather than compress them.

presentedReviews.rationale: Carrier describes the Pauline letters as speaking only of a celestial being and the gospels as literary fictions before using that sequence to conclude that the gospels first placed Jesus in history. Those disputed classifications already contain the developmental conclusion needing proof.
presentedReviews.context: Carrier’s documentary sequence labels Paul’s Jesus exclusively celestial and the later gospels fictional, then uses those labels to infer that historicization began with the gospels.

definition.label: Argument from ignorance
definition.definition: Treating a claim as true because it has not been disproved, or false because it has not been proved, rather than supplying positive evidence.

definition.label: Confirmation bias
definition.definition: Seeking, interpreting, or remembering evidence in ways that favor an existing view while discounting contrary information.

source.currentDescription: Carrier cites mythic formulas, scriptural rewrites, deliberate structures, etiologies, and improbable events to classify gospels as literary parables from which criteria cannot reliably extract history.
source.lockedProposition: Myth markers, scriptural rewrites, literary structures, and improbable events make the gospels unsuitable for extracting history.

source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Carrier links myth markers, deliberate literary architecture, Mosaic, Elijah, and Homeric rewritings, etiologies for baptism and eucharist, and central improbabilities to the inference that such constructed narratives resist straightforward extraction of an earthly biography. Principal limitation: The catalog names scholarship but compresses textual demonstrations, then moves from pervasive artistry and legendary development to the categorical conclusion that historical criteria recover nothing, although literary construction can preserve a historical subject. Live burden: He must compare concrete passages, explain why symbolism defeats rather than complicates particular historical inferences, and answer Evans’s verisimilitude claim without conflating allegory, myth, fiction, and improbability.

presentedReviews.rationale: Carrier assembles mythic formulas, scriptural rewrites, structures, etiologies, and improbable episodes to classify the gospels categorically as fiction while discounting the live alternative that highly constructed literature can preserve a historical subject. The evidence is interpreted consistently toward his prior literary-invention view.
presentedReviews.context: Carrier presents a one-directional inventory of gospel literary and mythic features and concludes that historical criteria can recover nothing from the narratives.

definition.label: Belief bias
definition.definition: Judging an argument by whether its conclusion feels believable instead of evaluating whether the conclusion follows from the premises.

source.lockedProposition: A Torah-shaped Jewish movement hostile to paganism is an unlikely setting for constructing a pagan composite messiah.

source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Evans tests Carrier’s diffusion mechanism against its Jewish social matrix, arguing that Torah observance, prophetic inheritance, redemption hopes, and abhorrence of Greco-Roman paganism make a composite pagan messiah culturally unexpected. Principal limitation: “Pagan Frankenstein” makes borrowing sound like deliberate wholesale assembly, while neither hostility nor generalized Jewish identity establishes how impermeable particular communities were to adapted influence. Live burden: Evans needs evidence about boundaries, transmission rates, and why scriptural reinterpretation could not naturalize outside motifs; Carrier must show that such contact produced a celestial Jesus rather than merely being possible.

presentedReviews.rationale: Evans calls the proposed borrowing culturally counterintuitive, but he supplies a reason involving Torah-centered hostility to paganism. The argument needs empirical support about cultural permeability; it is not merely acceptance of historicity because that conclusion feels believable.

Principal limitation: The comparison supports suspicion more securely than total excision, because brevity or disrupted continuity need not establish that every underlying notice is Christian, while calling the passage obvious and defenders desperate substitutes motive attribution for discriminating textual analysis. Live burden: He therefore still must exclude a minimally authentic notice later expanded by Christians and show that Josephus’s compositional variation cannot explain such compressed treatment.

presentedReviews.rationale: Carrier adduces positive contextual anomalies—terminology, narrative continuity, and Josephus’s handling of sects—for interpolation. The abbreviated case may be inconclusive, but it is not based merely on the notice’s authenticity having gone unproved.

definition.label: Appeal to authority
definition.definition: Relying on a person or institution's status as if it settles the argument, especially when the relevant evidence, expertise, or consensus has not been shown.

source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Evans meets the wholesale-interpolation objection with three linked details: lines in Antiquities 18 use non-Josephan vocabulary, the residue uses his normal diction, and that core explains the later incidental James notice within Ananus’s irregular execution and removal. Principal limitation: Citing Meier and scholarly agreement replaces examples of the vocabulary distribution, while the claim that Antiquities 20 presupposes the reconstructed earlier notice remains plausible rather than independently established here. Live burden: Evans still must show that the residual wording survived Christian transmission intact and gives genuinely independent attestation, not merely Josephus identifying figures already known through Christians.

presentedReviews.rationale: Evans invokes Meier’s reputation and mainstream agreement in place of supplying the claimed vocabulary distribution, making scholarly status materially carry the authentic-core conclusion.
presentedReviews.context: Evans cites John Meier’s credentials and scholarly agreement while defending Josephan vocabulary outside identified Christian interpolations.

definition.label: Begging the question
definition.definition: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.
